description:
Issue summary: AtlasDocs reported repeated p95/p99 latency waves and occasional request timeouts on short streaming requests. Impact: Customer-facing latencies exceeding SLA thresholds (p99 > 3s, intermittent 504s) for several hour windows across multiple nodes. Initial triage indicated spikes correlate with tenant resume/resumption patterns and internal prefetch activity.

Observed behavior: Short streaming requests that previously returned sub-400ms now intermittently hit 1.5-4s with a small fraction timing out (504). The pattern appears as a set of ~5-15 minute waves during which tail latency climbs then decays. Waves align to bursts of resumed streams from the same tenant and to periodic prefetch/eviction cycles in the KV cache layer.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer reproducer: Open 100 concurrent short streams (approx 15-50 tokens) with low steady QPS, then pause and resume a subset of streams after ~60s.
2) Observe batcher metrics: coalescing delay and flush frequency.
3) Monitor /api/v1/streams responses and token-latency histogram.
4) Reproduce in prod-us-east using AtlasDocs account id (provided in private logs).
investigation_notes:
Timeline: 2026-03-10 09:40 UTC first alert from AtlasDocs. Support confirmed customer impact and escalated to SRE.

Hypotheses tested: 
- H1: Batcher linger hysteresis alone (unlikely; similar to prior tickets but metrics show an additional queuing delay).
- H2: KV prefetch eviction/lock causing delayed coalesce flush when a resumed stream requires a prefetched slab (supported by correlation between prefetch mutex hold events and flush delay).
- H3: Tenant priority reweighting interaction (observed, but not primary).

Findings: Trace sampling shows a small number (~0.7%) of requests wait on a prefetch slab mutex for 200-1200ms just before flush, causing them to miss the regular microbatch and wait for the next scheduled flush. When many resumed streams hit the same slab, this amplifies into p95/p99 waves. Node restarts reduce occurrence temporarily.

Relevant artifacts: mutex contention spikes in /var/log/batcher/prefetch.log, heapster heap snapshots during wave, and a trace sample showing the hold sequence: accept -> prefetch-lock wait -> coalesce miss -> delayed flush -> timeout on client.

Temporary mitigations attempted: increased prefetch worker parallelism on a subset of dedicated nodes (reduced amplitude), disabled an aggressive prefetch eviction path (reduced occurrences but increased memory usage).
comments: Support (Asha): Customer noticed first around 09:30 UTC when a scheduled resume job ran. Provided sample request IDs and repro script.
SRE (Diego): Initial graphs show mutex hold spikes at the same timestamps as p99 spikes. Creating a targeted capture on two affected nodes. See Slack thread #support for live updates.

Eng (Maya Chen): Suggested a hypothesis around prefetch slab serialization; will instrument prefetch path to emit lock-hold durations and slab owner metadata. Working on a lightweight patch to short-circuit small-prefetch paths.
Customer (AtlasDocs/Ben): We see periodic user-facing freezes; any ETA for a fix? We're on dedicated capacity so impact is high for a subset of our endpoints.

SRE (Diego): Applied temporary config change to raise prefetch workers from 2 -> 6 for AtlasDocs pool at 2026-03-11T02:10Z. Observed reduction in p99 amplitude but side effect was memory pressure - rolled back partially.
Eng (Maya): Draft PR with an optimistic-trylock fallback: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4582 (WIP).
resolution:
Workaround: For AtlasDocs dedicated pool we temporarily adjusted prefetch concurrency and disabled aggressive eviction to break the slab contention pattern; this reduced p99 amplitude and eliminated timeouts while we validate a safer fix.

Planned fix: Engineering to merge optimistic-trylock fallback that avoids blocking coalesce on small prefetches, add metrics for prefetch-lock-hold-duration, and add a throttled fallback path that forces immediate flush when lock hold > 150ms. Target rollout: canary 2026-03-16, full rollout 2026-03-20 pending validation.

Follow-ups: Post-deploy smoke tests, add an automated alert on prefetch-lock-hold-duration > 100ms, and update continuous-batcher runbook with mitigation steps. Customer will be notified of planned maintenance and will receive a postmortem after full rollout.
